prompt: Which statements about Thiele–Small parameters are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: Factory tolerances on Vas can be ±20–30%, so measuring your own driver is worthwhile
options.explanation: Correct. Purdue's notes give that typical tolerance.

options.text: Fs is the frequency where the driver's impedance is lowest
options.explanation: At Fs the impedance peaks; the minimum is above it.

options.text: Qts is Qms × Qes divided by (Qms + Qes)
options.explanation: Correct. Total Q combines mechanical and electrical Q like resistors in parallel.

options.text: They describe the driver at small signal levels, where it behaves linearly
options.explanation: Correct. Large-signal behaviour (Xmax, thermal compression) needs other parameters.

workedExample:
- Qts combines the mechanical and electrical Q like resistors in parallel, so it is always below the smaller of the two. With a mechanical Q of 4 and an electrical Q of 0.4, it is about 0.36: the motor's electrical damping dominates.
- T/S parameters are small-signal values, measured from the impedance curve near resonance. Large-signal behaviour (Xmax, thermal compression) needs other parameters.
- Tolerances: about ±15% on Fs and ±20–30% on Vas (Purdue), so measuring your own driver is worthwhile.
- Impedance is at its maximum at Fs and has its minimum above it.
